# Rollout And Compatibility Plan

Status: **Frozen**
Date: 2026-03-08
Phase: P0-W4
Depends on: P0-W1 (V2 Architecture RFC), P0-W2 (Target Model Spec), P0-W3 (Network Model)

This document defines the staged rollout strategy for transitioning Spectraplex
from its current wallet-centric V1 architecture to the target-centric V2
architecture. It covers the compatibility window, old-to-new schema mapping,
deprecation sequence, per-packet compatibility strategies, and the test matrix
during transition.

The primary inputs are:
- P0-W1 Sections 11-12 (dual-write strategy, deprecation sequence)
- P0-W2 Section 11 (downstream packet mapping, target registration needs)
- P0-W3 Section 6 (legacy checkpoint migration guidance)
- Current codebase at commit `33205bb` (tip of `main`)

---

## 1. Compatibility Window

### 1.1 Definition

The compatibility window is the period during which both V1 (wallet-centric) and
V2 (target-centric) code paths coexist. During this window:

- All current wallet-facing API endpoints continue to work unchanged
- All current CLI commands and flags continue to work unchanged
- All current database tables remain intact and receive writes
- New V2 tables and code paths are added alongside, not in place of, V1

### 1.2 Window Boundaries

| Milestone | Phase | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Window opens** | P1-W2 | First V2 migration lands (new tables alongside old) |
| **Dual-write active** | P1-W4 | Repository writes to both V1 and V2 tables |
| **Dual-read available** | P2-W2 | New target-scoped read paths exist; V1 reads still primary |
| **V1 reads redirected** | P2-W6 | Wallet-scoped reads optionally route through V2 tables |
| **V1 writes deprecated** | Phase 3+ | V1 tables become read-only compatibility views |
| **Window closes** | Phase 4+ | V1 tables can be dropped (requires explicit user approval) |

### 1.3 Invariants During Compatibility Window

These must hold true for the entire duration:

1. `cargo test --workspace` passes at every commit
2. `cargo fmt --all --check` passes at every commit
3. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes at every commit
4. Existing wallet API endpoints return identical response shapes
5. Existing CLI commands accept the same flags and produce the same behavior
6. No data loss during the transition — every V1 write is also captured in V2
7. Rollback is possible by removing dual-write and reverting to V1-only paths

---

## 2. Old-To-New Schema Mapping

### 2.1 Table-Level Mapping

| V1 Table | V2 Replacement | Migration Strategy |
|---|---|---|
| `transactions` | `raw_transactions` + `target_matches` | Additive; `transactions` kept during window |
| `ledger_entries` | `ledger_entries` (unchanged initially) | Unchanged in Phase 1-2; derived from Silver datasets in Phase 3 |
| `indexer_checkpoints` | `checkpoints` | Additive; both written during dual-write |
| `blocks` | `raw_blocks` | Rename/migrate in P1-W2; keep old if data exists |
| `evm_logs` | `raw_evm_logs` | Rename/migrate in P1-W2; keep old if data exists |
| `hl_fills` | `raw_hl_events` (superset) | Additive; `hl_fills` kept initially |
| (none) | `networks` | New table, seeded in P1-W2 |
| (none) | `index_targets` | New table |
| (none) | `target_matches` | New table |
| (none) | `ingestion_runs` | New table |
| (none) | `dataset_versions` | New table |

### 2.2 Column-Level Mapping: `transactions` → `raw_transactions`

| V1 Column (`transactions`) | V2 Column (`raw_transactions`) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (UUID PK) | `id` (UUID PK) | Direct mapping |
| `user_id` (UUID NOT NULL) | (removed) | Replaced by `index_targets.owner_id` |
| `wallet_address` (VARCHAR NOT NULL) | (removed) | Replaced by `target_matches` join |
| `timestamp` (BIGINT) | `timestamp` (BIGINT) | Direct mapping |
| `tx_hash` (VARCHAR NOT NULL) | `tx_hash` (TEXT NOT NULL) | Direct mapping |
| `chain` (chain_enum) | `network` (TEXT, FK to networks) | See Section 2.4 |
| `raw_metadata` (JSONB) | `raw_metadata` (JSONB) | Direct mapping |
| `created_at` (TIMESTAMPTZ) | `ingested_at` (TIMESTAMPTZ) | Rename for clarity |
| (none) | `ingestion_run_id` (UUID, FK) | New provenance field |
| (none) | `source` (TEXT) | "rpc", "grpc", "rest", "ws" |
| (none) | `block_number` (BIGINT) | Extracted for indexed access |

### 2.3 Column-Level Mapping: `indexer_checkpoints` → `checkpoints`

| V1 Column | V2 Column | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `chain` (chain_enum) | (removed, derived from network) | See P0-W3 Section 6 |
| `wallet_address` (TEXT) | `target_id` (UUID, FK) | Wallet becomes an index target |
| `last_signature` (TEXT) | `cursor.last_signature` (JSONB) | Nested in JSONB cursor |
| `last_slot` (BIGINT) | `cursor.last_slot` (JSONB) | Nested in JSONB cursor |
| `last_block` (BIGINT) | `cursor.last_block` (JSONB) | Nested in JSONB cursor |
| `last_timestamp` (BIGINT) | `cursor.last_timestamp_ms` (JSONB) | Multiply by 1000 per P0-W3 Section 6.3 |
| `updated_at` (TIMESTAMPTZ) | `updated_at` (TIMESTAMPTZ) | Direct mapping |
| (none) | `network` (TEXT) | New dimension |
| (none) | `source` (TEXT) | "rpc", "grpc", "rest", "ws" |

### 2.4 Chain-to-Network Mapping

From P0-W3 Section 6.5:

| V1 `chain` value | V2 `chain_family` | V2 default `network` | V2 default `source` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `solana` | `solana` | `solana-mainnet` | `rpc` |
| `hyperliquid` | `hyperliquid` | `hypercore-mainnet` | `rest` |
| `ethereum` | `evm` | `ethereum-mainnet` | `rpc` |

**Caveat (from P0-W3 Section 6.4):** If a deployment indexed Base, Arbitrum, or
other EVM chain data under `Chain::Ethereum`, those rows will be incorrectly
assigned to `ethereum-mainnet`. The reclassification mechanism is deferred to
P1-W2.

### 2.5 Enum Type Mapping

| V1 Enum | V2 Replacement | Migration |
|---|---|---|
| `chain_enum` ('solana', 'hyperliquid', 'ethereum') | `chain_family_enum` ('solana', 'evm', 'hyperliquid') + `networks` table | Additive; old enum kept |
| `entry_type_enum` | Unchanged | No change needed in Phase 1-2 |

### 2.6 Core Rust Type Mapping

| V1 Type | V2 Type | Coexistence Strategy |
|---|---|---|
| `Chain` enum | `ChainFamily` enum + `Network` type | Both exist; `Chain` kept for V1 compat |
| `Transaction` struct | `RawRecord` struct (no `user_id`/`wallet_address`) | Both exist; adapter produces both during dual-write |
| `IndexerCheckpoint` struct | `Checkpoint` struct (JSONB cursor) | Both exist; repo writes both |
| `ChainIngestor` trait | `Connector` trait | Both exist; `ChainIngestor` wraps `Connector` |
| `LedgerEntry` struct | Unchanged initially | Modified in Phase 3 |
| `EntryType` enum | Unchanged | No change needed |

---

## 3. Deprecation Sequence

This sequence is consistent with P0-W1 Section 12.

### 3.1 Phase 1 Deprecations (Soft — New Alternatives Added)

| Element | Status | Replacement | When Safe To Remove |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Transaction.user_id` field | Soft-deprecated | `index_targets.owner_id` | Phase 2+ |
| `Transaction.wallet_address` field | Soft-deprecated | `target_matches` join | Phase 2+ |
| `Chain` enum | Soft-deprecated | `ChainFamily` + `Network` | Phase 2+ |
| `ChainIngestor` trait | Soft-deprecated | `Connector` trait | Phase 2+ |

"Soft-deprecated" means: the old type/field still exists and functions, but new
code should use the V2 replacement. No compile warnings are added yet.

### 3.2 Phase 2 Deprecations (Active — V2 Paths Preferred)

| Element | Status | Replacement | When Safe To Remove |
|---|---|---|---|
| `transactions.wallet_address` column | Write-only compat | `target_matches` | Phase 3+ |
| `transactions.user_id` column | Write-only compat | `index_targets.owner_id` | Phase 3+ |
| `indexer_checkpoints` table | Write-only compat | `checkpoints` table | Phase 3+ |
| `ChainIngestor::fetch_history` | Wrapper only | `Connector::backfill` | Phase 3+ |

"Write-only compat" means: the old path still receives writes via dual-write,
but reads are migrating to V2 tables. The old path is no longer the source of
truth.

### 3.3 Phase 3+ Deprecations (Removal Candidates)

| Element | Status | Prerequisite For Removal |
|---|---|---|
| `transactions` table | Drop candidate | All reads migrated to `raw_transactions` + `target_matches` |
| `indexer_checkpoints` table | Drop candidate | All reads migrated to `checkpoints` |
| `Chain` enum (Rust) | Remove candidate | All code uses `ChainFamily` + `Network` |
| `chain_enum` (SQL) | Drop candidate | No tables reference it |
| Wallet-only API routes | Redirect candidate | Target-scoped routes fully functional |
| Wallet-only CLI flags | Redirect candidate | Target-scoped flags fully functional |

### 3.4 Elements That Are NOT Deprecated

| Element | Reason |
|---|---|
| `ledger_entries` table | Stays as a Silver dataset; schema may evolve but table persists |
| `entry_type_enum` | Still valid for ledger classification |
| Wallet as a target kind | First-class target kind permanently |
| `/v1/transactions/:wallet` route shape | Remains valid; implementation may route through V2 tables |
| `/v1/ledger/:wallet` route shape | Remains valid |
| `blocks` / `evm_logs` / `hl_fills` tables | May be renamed to `raw_*` but data preserved |

---

## 4. Per-Packet Compatibility Strategy

Every Phase 1 and Phase 2 work packet has an identified compatibility strategy
below. Phase 3-5 packets are included for completeness.

### 4.1 Phase 1 Packets

#### P1-W1: Introduce V2 Core Types

**Compatibility strategy:** Additive types only. No existing types are modified
or removed. New types (`ChainFamily`, `Network`, `IndexTarget`, `TargetKind`,
`RawRecord`, `Checkpoint`, `IngestionRun`, `Connector` trait) are added
alongside existing types.

**What stays unchanged:**
- `Chain` enum
- `Transaction` struct
- `IndexerCheckpoint` struct
- `ChainIngestor` trait
- `LedgerEntry` struct
- `EntryType` enum

**Test impact:** Existing tests pass unmodified. New unit tests added for V2
type serialization and parsing.

#### P1-W2: Add New Bronze And Control-Plane Tables

**Compatibility strategy:** Additive migrations only. New tables are created
alongside existing tables. No existing table is altered or dropped. The
`chain_family_enum`, `target_kind_enum`, and `target_mode_enum` SQL types are
created as new types (not modifications to `chain_enum`).

**What stays unchanged:**
- `transactions` table and all its columns, indexes, and constraints
- `ledger_entries` table
- `indexer_checkpoints` table
- `blocks`, `evm_logs`, `hl_fills` tables
- `chain_enum`, `entry_type_enum` SQL types

**Migration safety:**
- Migrations must apply cleanly on an empty database
- Migrations must apply cleanly on top of the current V1 schema
- No `ALTER TABLE` on existing tables
- No `DROP` of existing objects

**Test impact:** Migration test verifies both fresh and upgrade paths.

#### P1-W3: Repository Support For Canonical Raw Data

**Compatibility strategy:** New repository methods added alongside existing
ones. No existing method signature is changed. The `SpectralRepo` (or
equivalent) struct gains new methods for V2 tables without modifying existing
method bodies.

**What stays unchanged:**
- All wallet-scoped read methods (`get_transactions_by_wallet`, etc.)
- All wallet-scoped write methods (`save_transactions`, etc.)
- All checkpoint methods (`get_checkpoint`, `save_checkpoint`, etc.)

**Test impact:** Existing repository tests pass unmodified. New tests added for
V2 methods.

#### P1-W4: Dual-Write Compatibility Layer

**Compatibility strategy:** This is the critical compatibility packet. The
repository layer is modified so that every write that currently goes to V1 tables
ALSO writes to V2 tables. The dual-write is implemented in the repository
layer, not in adapters or handlers.

**Dual-write flow (from P0-W1 Section 11.2):**
```
Ingestion request (wallet-shaped)
  |-- [compat shim] create IndexTarget(kind=wallet) if not exists
  |-- [compat shim] use old ChainIngestor::fetch_history
  |
  +-- write to `transactions` (V1)
  +-- write to `raw_transactions` (V2)
  +-- write to `target_matches` (V2)
  +-- write to `checkpoints` (V2)
  +-- write to `indexer_checkpoints` (V1)
```

**What stays unchanged:**
- All API handler signatures and response shapes
- All CLI command signatures and flags
- All adapter `fetch_history` signatures
- Read paths continue to use V1 tables

**Failure mode:** If the V2 write fails, the V1 write should still succeed (V2
write is best-effort during early transition). Once V2 writes are proven stable,
the V1 write becomes the best-effort side.

**Test impact:**
- Existing tests pass unmodified
- New tests verify that both V1 and V2 tables receive data
- New tests verify that a V1-only read returns the same data as before

#### P1-W5: Migration And Rollback Verification

**Compatibility strategy:** Verification-only packet. Validates that:
- Fresh DB migrations produce a valid combined V1+V2 schema
- Upgraded DB migrations apply cleanly on top of existing V1 data
- Uniqueness constraints work across both schema generations
- A single raw transaction can match multiple targets
- Rollback scenario: V2 tables can be dropped without affecting V1 tables

**Test impact:** Dedicated migration test suite.

### 4.2 Phase 2 Packets

#### P2-W1: Connector Interface Redesign

**Compatibility strategy:** The new `Connector` trait is added alongside the
existing `ChainIngestor` trait. A compatibility adapter wraps each existing
`ChainIngestor` implementation as a `Connector` that:
- Accepts `IndexTarget(kind=wallet)` and delegates to `fetch_history`
- Produces `RawRecord` from the `Transaction` output
- Returns V2 `Checkpoint` from the legacy checkpoint data

**What stays unchanged:**
- `ChainIngestor` trait definition and all implementations
- All existing adapter modules (`solana.rs`, `evm.rs`, `hyperliquid.rs`, etc.)

**Test impact:** New tests verify connector wrapper produces correct output.
Existing adapter tests pass unmodified.

#### P2-W2: CLI And API Target Registration Flow

**Compatibility strategy:** New endpoints and CLI commands are added alongside
existing ones. Existing wallet-shaped requests are accepted as before and
internally create wallet targets via the compatibility shim.

**New API endpoints (additive):**
- `POST /v1/targets` — register a target
- `GET /v1/targets` — list targets
- `GET /v1/targets/:target_id` — get target details
- `POST /v1/targets/:target_id/ingest` — start ingestion for a target

**New CLI flags (additive):**
- `--target-kind` — specify target kind
- `--target-address` — specify target address
- `--network` — specify network

**What stays unchanged:**
- `POST /v1/ingest` still accepts `{ chain, wallet, user_id? }`
- `POST /v1/ingest/batch` still accepts `{ wallets: [...] }`
- `--wallet` CLI flag still works

**Test impact:** Existing API and CLI tests pass unmodified. New tests for
target registration flow.

#### P2-W3: Fix EVM Ingestion Semantics

**Compatibility strategy:** The EVM adapter gains target-aware ingestion paths.
The existing `fetch_history(wallet, ...)` path is preserved as a compatibility
wrapper that:
- Creates a wallet target internally
- Uses the correct EVM ingestion strategy for wallets (ERC-20 Transfer logs by
  from/to topics, not contract address filter)
- Continues to produce `Transaction` structs for V1 compat

**New capabilities added:**
- Contract target: `eth_getLogs` with contract address (existing behavior, now
  correctly labeled)
- Wallet target: ERC-20 Transfer log scanning by from/to indexed parameters
- Topic filter target: arbitrary topic-based log scanning

**What stays unchanged:**
- `fetch_history` method signature
- All existing tests (output may change if the wallet path is corrected — see
  note below)

**Important note:** Correcting EVM wallet ingestion semantics means the wallet
path will return DIFFERENT (more correct) data. This is a semantic fix, not a
regression. The compatibility strategy preserves the API surface, not the
(currently incorrect) data content.

#### P2-W4: Fix Solana gRPC Target Semantics

**Compatibility strategy:** The Solana gRPC adapter gains target-aware
subscription filters. The existing `fetch_history(wallet, ...)` path is
preserved as a compatibility wrapper that:
- Creates a wallet target internally
- Uses `account_include` with the wallet pubkey (not program IDs)
- Stops stamping arbitrary wallet identity onto program-filtered results

**New capabilities added:**
- Program target: `account_include = [program_id]` subscription
- Account target: `account_include = [account_pubkey]` subscription
- Wallet target: `account_include = [wallet_pubkey]` subscription

**What stays unchanged:**
- `fetch_history` method signature for backward compatibility
- CLI gRPC path behavior when called with `--wallet`

#### P2-W5: Hyperliquid Target Model

**Compatibility strategy:** The Hyperliquid adapters (REST and WS) gain
target-aware paths. The existing wallet/user path is preserved unchanged.

**New capabilities added:**
- Market target: market-scoped REST/WS APIs
- HyperEVM target: routes to EVM connector with `hyperevm-mainnet` network

**What stays unchanged:**
- `fetch_history` for wallet/user targets
- All existing Hyperliquid adapter code
- WebSocket subscription behavior for user events

#### P2-W6: End-To-End Ingestion Compatibility Suite

**Compatibility strategy:** This is a verification-only packet. It adds
integration tests that verify:
- Wallet targets work through both V1 and V2 paths
- New target types (contract, program, market) work through V2 paths
- Dual-write produces consistent data in both table generations
- Checkpoints are consistent between V1 and V2

### 4.3 Phase 3 Packets

#### P3-W1: Dataset Registry And Versioning

**Compatibility:** Additive tables and types only. No impact on existing flows.

#### P3-W2: Transfer And Balance-Delta Datasets

**Compatibility:** New Silver tables alongside existing `ledger_entries`. No
existing table altered.

#### P3-W3: Event And Instruction Datasets

**Compatibility:** New Silver tables. Existing `evm_logs` and `hl_fills` data
preserved.

#### P3-W4: Hyperliquid Reusable Datasets

**Compatibility:** Fills, funding, positions as new tables. Existing `hl_fills`
data preserved or migrated.

#### P3-W5: Ledger As A Derived Materialization

**Compatibility:** `ledger_entries` table and API response shapes preserved.
Internal generation logic changes to read from Silver datasets instead of raw
transactions directly.

#### P3-W6: Completeness Metadata

**Compatibility:** Additive metadata tables and fields. No impact on existing
flows.

### 4.4 Phase 4 Packets

#### P4-W1: Dataset Query API

**Compatibility:** New endpoints alongside existing wallet-scoped ones.

#### P4-W2: Export Jobs

**Compatibility:** New export capabilities. Existing CSV export preserved.

#### P4-W3: Sink Abstraction

**Compatibility:** New delivery channels. No impact on existing API.

#### P4-W4: Metadata And Observability

**Compatibility:** Additive metadata on exports. No breaking changes.

#### P4-W5: Compatibility Pass

**Compatibility:** Final verification that V1 wallet paths still function after
all V2 changes.

### 4.5 Phase 5 Packets

#### P5-W1: Wallet / Tax / Forensics Pack

**Compatibility:** Builds on V2 infrastructure. V1 paths may be sunset after
this pack proves the V2 replacements.

#### P5-W2: Hyperliquid Analytics Pack

**Compatibility:** New downstream materialization. No V1 impact.

#### P5-W3: Protocol / TVL Pack

**Compatibility:** New downstream materialization. No V1 impact.

---

## 5. Test Matrix During Transition

### 5.1 Test Categories

| Category | Description | When Run |
|---|---|---|
| **Unit** | Rust type tests, serialization, parsing | Every commit |
| **Migration-fresh** | Apply all migrations to empty DB | Every commit with migration changes |
| **Migration-upgrade** | Apply new migrations on top of V1 schema with data | Every commit with migration changes |
| **Dual-write** | Verify both V1 and V2 tables receive writes | P1-W4 onward |
| **Dual-read** | Verify V1 reads return same data as V2 reads | P2-W2 onward |
| **V1-compat** | Verify all existing API/CLI behavior unchanged | Every commit |
| **V2-functional** | Verify new target-scoped paths work | P1-W3 onward |
| **Rollback** | Verify V2 tables can be dropped without V1 impact | P1-W5 |
| **Cross-target** | Verify one raw tx can link to multiple targets | P1-W4 onward |
| **Checkpoint-migration** | Verify legacy checkpoint → V2 checkpoint conversion | P1-W4 |

### 5.2 Test Matrix By Phase

#### Phase 1 Test Matrix

| Test | P1-W1 | P1-W2 | P1-W3 | P1-W4 | P1-W5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unit (V2 types) | ✓ | | | | |
| Migration-fresh | | ✓ | | | ✓ |
| Migration-upgrade | | ✓ | | | ✓ |
| Repo V2 methods | | | ✓ | | |
| Dual-write | | | | ✓ | ✓ |
| V1-compat (API) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| V1-compat (CLI) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Cross-target | | | | ✓ | ✓ |
| Checkpoint-migration | | | | ✓ | ✓ |
| Rollback | | | | | ✓ |

#### Phase 2 Test Matrix

| Test | P2-W1 | P2-W2 | P2-W3 | P2-W4 | P2-W5 | P2-W6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Connector wrapper | ✓ | | | | | |
| Target registration | | ✓ | | | | |
| EVM wallet target | | | ✓ | | | ✓ |
| EVM contract target | | | ✓ | | | ✓ |

| Dual-write | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Dual-read | | ✓ | | | | ✓ |
| V1-compat (full) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

### 5.3 Dual-Write Test Scenarios

These scenarios must be covered by P1-W4 and maintained through Phase 2:

| Scenario | Description | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| **DW-1** | Ingest a Solana wallet transaction via V1 path | Row appears in both `transactions` and `raw_transactions`; `target_matches` links the wallet target |
| **DW-2** | Ingest same tx for two wallets | One `raw_transactions` row, two `target_matches` rows, two `transactions` rows |
| **DW-3** | Checkpoint save via V1 path | Row appears in both `indexer_checkpoints` and `checkpoints` |
| **DW-4** | Resume from checkpoint via V1 path | Legacy checkpoint fields produce correct resume behavior |
| **DW-5** | V2-only write (new target type) | Row appears in `raw_transactions` + `target_matches`; no `transactions` row |
| **DW-6** | V1 write fails, V2 succeeds | V2 data is preserved; V1 failure is logged but not fatal |
| **DW-7** | V2 write fails, V1 succeeds | V1 data is preserved; V2 failure is logged but not fatal (early transition only) |

### 5.4 Dual-Read Test Scenarios

These scenarios apply from P2-W2 onward:

| Scenario | Description | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| **DR-1** | `GET /v1/transactions/:wallet` via V1 tables | Returns expected transactions |
| **DR-2** | `GET /v1/transactions/:wallet` via V2 tables (target_matches join) | Returns same data as DR-1 |
| **DR-3** | `GET /v1/ledger/:wallet` via V1 tables | Returns expected ledger entries |
| **DR-4** | `GET /v1/ledger/:wallet` via V2 tables | Returns same data as DR-3 |
| **DR-5** | `GET /v1/balances/:wallet` via V1 tables | Returns expected balances |
| **DR-6** | `GET /v1/balances/:wallet` via V2 tables | Returns same data as DR-5 |
| **DR-7** | `GET /v1/stats/:wallet` via V1 tables | Returns expected stats |
| **DR-8** | `GET /v1/stats/:wallet` via V2 tables | Returns same data as DR-7 |

### 5.5 Migration Test Scenarios

| Scenario | Description | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| **MG-1** | Apply all migrations to empty PostgreSQL | All tables exist, all constraints valid |
| **MG-2** | Apply V2 migrations on top of V1 schema (no data) | Clean application, no errors |
| **MG-3** | Apply V2 migrations on top of V1 schema with data | Data preserved, V1 tables untouched |
| **MG-4** | Legacy Solana checkpoint → V2 checkpoint | `last_signature` → `cursor.last_signature`, `last_slot` → `cursor.last_slot`, `source = "rpc"`, `network = "solana-mainnet"` |
| **MG-5** | Legacy HyperCore checkpoint → V2 checkpoint | `last_timestamp * 1000` → `cursor.last_timestamp_ms`, `source = "rest"`, `network = "hypercore-mainnet"` |
| **MG-6** | Legacy EVM checkpoint → V2 checkpoint | `last_block` → `cursor.last_block`, `source = "rpc"`, `network = "ethereum-mainnet"` |
| **MG-7** | Drop V2 tables (rollback) | V1 tables still function, no FK violations |

---

## 6. Compatibility Shim Design

### 6.1 Wallet-to-Target Shim

When a V1 wallet-shaped request arrives (API or CLI), the compatibility shim:

1. Looks up `index_targets` for `(kind=wallet, network=<derived>, address=<wallet>)`
2. If not found, creates an `IndexTarget` with:
   - `kind = wallet`
   - `network` derived from the `chain` parameter using Section 2.4 mapping
   - `chain_family` derived from the network
   - `address = <wallet_address>`
   - `mode = backfill` (or `both` if streaming)
   - `owner_id` set from `user_id` if provided (nullable)
3. Returns the target ID for use in V2 write paths

### 6.2 Transaction-to-RawRecord Shim

When the adapter produces a V1 `Transaction` struct, the shim creates a V2
`RawRecord` by:

1. Copying `id`, `timestamp`, `tx_hash`, `raw_metadata`
2. Mapping `chain` to `network` (Section 2.4)
3. Discarding `user_id` and `wallet_address` (these are captured via
   `target_matches` and `index_targets.owner_id`)
4. Adding `source` based on the adapter type

### 6.3 Checkpoint Shim

When the repo writes a V1 `indexer_checkpoints` row, the shim also writes a V2
`checkpoints` row by:

1. Looking up the wallet target from Section 6.1
2. Building a JSONB cursor from the legacy fields (per P0-W3 Section 6)
3. Setting `network` from Section 2.4 mapping
4. Setting `source` from the adapter type

---

## 7. Risk Register

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dual-write performance overhead | Medium | Medium | Benchmark; batch V2 writes; use same transaction where possible |
| V1/V2 data drift during transition | Low | High | Reconciliation tests in P1-W5 and P2-W6 |
| EVM network reclassification for multi-chain deployments | Medium | Medium | P1-W2 must define override mechanism (P0-W3 Section 6.4) |
| HyperCore timestamp precision loss on first resume | Low | Low | Existing dedup on `(network, tx_hash)` handles re-fetches (P0-W3 Section 6.3) |
| Legacy gRPC Solana checkpoints assigned to wrong source | Low | Low | Default `source = "rpc"` is safe for resume; gRPC gets fresh checkpoints (P0-W3 Section 6.2) |
| Schema complexity during mid-transition | Medium | Low | Clear table naming; design docs; migration comments |

---

## 8. Rollback Strategy

### 8.1 Phase 1 Rollback

If Phase 1 V2 changes need to be rolled back:

1. Remove dual-write logic from repository layer (revert P1-W4)
2. V2 tables can be dropped without affecting V1 tables (no FKs from V1 to V2)
3. V2 Rust types can be feature-gated or removed
4. All V1 paths continue to function as before

### 8.2 Phase 2 Rollback

If Phase 2 changes need to be rolled back:

1. Remove new API endpoints and CLI flags (additive, so removal is clean)
2. Remove connector wrappers; restore direct `ChainIngestor` usage
3. Dual-write can be disabled; V1 tables still have all data
4. Any semantic corrections to adapters (EVM, Solana gRPC) should be evaluated
   individually — some corrections are improvements regardless of V2

### 8.3 Point of No Return

The compatibility window closes (and rollback becomes impractical) once:

- V1 `transactions` table stops receiving writes
- Read paths are fully migrated to V2 tables
- V1 tables are dropped

This does not happen until Phase 4+ and requires explicit user approval.

---

### 9.1 P0-W1 (V2 Architecture RFC) Dependencies

| P0-W1 Section | Used In This Doc |

| Section 11 (Dual-Write Strategy) | Sections 2, 4.1 (P1-W4), 5.3, 6 |

### 9.2 P0-W2 (Target Model Spec) Dependencies

| Section 2.1 (wallet kind) | Section 6.1 (wallet-to-target shim) |
| Section 3 (Validity Matrix) | Section 4.2 (P2-W3, P2-W4, P2-W5 target support) |
| Section 6 (Uniqueness Rules) | Section 6.1 (target dedup) |
| Section 7 (Ownership Rules) | Section 6.1 (owner_id mapping) |
| Section 11 (Downstream Mapping) | Section 4 (per-packet strategies) |

| Section 1 (Network Registry) | Section 2.4 (chain-to-network mapping) |

## 1. Compatibility Window

### 1.1 Window Boundaries

| Milestone | Phase | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Window opens** | P1-W2 | First V2 migration lands (new tables alongside old) |
| **Dual-write active** | P1-W4 | Repository writes to both V1 and V2 tables |

### 1.2 Invariants

These must hold true for the entire duration of the compatibility window:

1. `cargo test --workspace` passes at every commit
2. `cargo fmt --all --check` passes at every commit

| (none) | `index_targets` | New table |
| (none) | `target_matches` | New table |
| (none) | `ingestion_runs` | New table |
| (none) | `dataset_versions` | New table |

### 2.2 Column Mapping: `transactions` → `raw_transactions`

| `user_id` (UUID NOT NULL) | (removed) | Replaced by `index_targets.owner_id` |

| `ledger_entries` table | Stays as Silver dataset |
| `entry_type_enum` | Still valid for ledger classification |
| Wallet as a target kind | First-class target kind permanently |
| `/v1/transactions/:wallet` route shape | Remains valid; may route through V2 internally |
| `/v1/ledger/:wallet` route shape | Remains valid |

---

## 4. Per-Packet Compatibility Strategy

Every Phase 1 and Phase 2 work packet has an identified compatibility strategy.

### 4.1 Phase 1 Packets

#### P1-W1: Introduce V2 Core Types

**Strategy:** Additive types only. No existing types modified or removed. New
types (`ChainFamily`, `Network`, `IndexTarget`, `TargetKind`, `RawRecord`,
`Checkpoint`, `IngestionRun`, `Connector` trait) added alongside existing types.

**Unchanged:** `Chain`, `Transaction`, `IndexerCheckpoint`, `ChainIngestor`,
`LedgerEntry`, `EntryType`.

#### P1-W2: Add New Bronze And Control-Plane Tables

**Strategy:** Additive migrations only. New tables created alongside existing
tables. No existing table altered or dropped. New SQL enum types
(`chain_family_enum`, `target_kind_enum`, `target_mode_enum`) created as
separate types, not modifications to `chain_enum`.

**Unchanged:** All existing tables, columns, indexes, constraints, and enum types.

**Migration safety:** Must apply cleanly on empty DB and on top of current V1
schema. No `ALTER TABLE` on existing tables. No `DROP`.

#### P1-W3: Repository Support For Canonical Raw Data

**Strategy:** New repository methods added alongside existing ones. No existing
method signature changed.

**Unchanged:** All wallet-scoped read/write methods.

#### P1-W4: Dual-Write Compatibility Layer

**Strategy:** Repository layer modified so every V1 write also writes to V2
tables. The dual-write boundary is in the repository layer, not in adapters or
handlers.

**Dual-write flow (from P0-W1 Section 11.2):**
```
Ingestion request (wallet-shaped)
  |-- [compat shim] create IndexTarget(kind=wallet) if not exists
  |-- [compat shim] use old ChainIngestor::fetch_history
  |
  +-- write to `transactions` (V1)
  +-- write to `raw_transactions` (V2)
  +-- write to `target_matches` (V2)
  +-- write to `checkpoints` (V2)
  +-- write to `indexer_checkpoints` (V1)
```

**Unchanged:** All API handler signatures/responses. All CLI command
signatures/flags. All adapter `fetch_history` signatures. Read paths continue
to use V1 tables.

**Failure mode:** During early transition, V2 write failure does not block V1
write. Once V2 writes are proven stable, V1 write becomes best-effort.

#### P1-W5: Migration And Rollback Verification

**Strategy:** Verification-only packet. Validates fresh-DB and upgrade-DB
migration paths, cross-target linking, and rollback safety.

### 4.2 Phase 2 Packets

#### P2-W1: Connector Interface Redesign

**Strategy:** New `Connector` trait added alongside `ChainIngestor`. A
compatibility adapter wraps each `ChainIngestor` as a `Connector` that accepts
`IndexTarget(kind=wallet)` and delegates to `fetch_history`.

**Unchanged:** `ChainIngestor` trait and all implementations.

#### P2-W2: CLI And API Target Registration Flow

**Strategy:** New API endpoints and CLI flags added alongside existing ones.
Existing wallet-shaped requests accepted as before and internally create wallet
targets via compatibility shim.

**New endpoints (additive):** `POST /v1/targets`, `GET /v1/targets`,
`GET /v1/targets/:target_id`, `POST /v1/targets/:target_id/ingest`.

**New CLI flags (additive):** `--target-kind`, `--target-address`, `--network`.

**Unchanged:** `POST /v1/ingest`, `POST /v1/ingest/batch`, `--wallet` CLI flag.

#### P2-W3: Fix EVM Ingestion Semantics

**Strategy:** EVM adapter gains target-aware paths. Existing `fetch_history`
preserved as compatibility wrapper. Note: correcting EVM wallet semantics
changes data content (more correct results), not API surface.

**Unchanged:** `fetch_history` method signature.

#### P2-W4: Fix Solana gRPC Target Semantics

**Strategy:** Solana gRPC adapter gains target-aware subscription filters.
Existing `fetch_history` preserved as compatibility wrapper. Stops stamping
arbitrary wallet identity onto program-filtered results.

**Unchanged:** `fetch_history` method signature for backward compatibility.

#### P2-W5: Hyperliquid Target Model

**Strategy:** Hyperliquid adapters gain target-aware paths. Existing wallet/user
path preserved unchanged. Market targets and HyperEVM routing added as new
capabilities.

**Unchanged:** `fetch_history` for wallet/user targets.

#### P2-W6: End-To-End Ingestion Compatibility Suite

**Strategy:** Verification-only packet. Integration tests verify wallet targets
through V1 and V2 paths, new target types through V2 paths, dual-write
consistency, and checkpoint consistency.

---

## 5. Test Matrix

### 5.1 Categories

| Category | Description | When Run |
|---|---|---|
| **Unit** | Rust type tests, serialization, parsing | Every commit |
| **Migration-fresh** | All migrations on empty DB | Migration changes |
| **Migration-upgrade** | New migrations on V1 schema with data | Migration changes |
| **Dual-write** | Both V1 and V2 tables receive writes | P1-W4 onward |
| **Dual-read** | V1 reads match V2 reads | P2-W2 onward |
| **V1-compat** | All existing API/CLI behavior unchanged | Every commit |
| **V2-functional** | New target-scoped paths work | P1-W3 onward |
| **Rollback** | V2 tables droppable without V1 impact | P1-W5 |
| **Cross-target** | One raw tx links to multiple targets | P1-W4 onward |
| **Checkpoint-migration** | Legacy → V2 checkpoint conversion | P1-W4 |

### 5.2 Phase 1 Test Matrix

| Unit (V2 types) | ✓ | | | | |
| Migration-fresh | | ✓ | | | ✓ |

| V1-compat (CLI) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

### 5.3 Phase 2 Test Matrix

### 5.4 Dual-Write Test Scenarios

| MG-4 | Solana checkpoint migration | `last_signature` → `cursor.last_signature`, `source = "rpc"`, `network = "solana-mainnet"` |
| MG-5 | HyperCore checkpoint migration | `last_timestamp * 1000` → `cursor.last_timestamp_ms`, `source = "rest"`, `network = "hypercore-mainnet"` |
| MG-6 | EVM checkpoint migration | `last_block` → `cursor.last_block`, `source = "rpc"`, `network = "ethereum-mainnet"` |
| MG-7 | Drop V2 tables (rollback) | V1 tables still function, no FK violations |

---

## 6. Compatibility Shim Design

### 6.1 Wallet-to-Target Shim

When a V1 wallet-shaped request arrives:

1. Look up `index_targets` for `(kind=wallet, network=<derived>, address=<wallet>)`
2. If not found, create with `kind = wallet`, `network` from chain mapping
   (Section 2.4), `chain_family` derived from network, `address = <wallet>`,
   `mode = backfill`, `owner_id` from `user_id` if provided
3. Return target ID for V2 write paths

### 6.2 Transaction-to-RawRecord Shim

When adapter produces V1 `Transaction`:

1. Copy `id`, `timestamp`, `tx_hash`, `raw_metadata`
2. Map `chain` → `network` (Section 2.4)
3. Discard `user_id` and `wallet_address` (captured via `target_matches` and
   `index_targets.owner_id`)
4. Add `source` from adapter type

### 6.3 Checkpoint Shim

When repo writes V1 `indexer_checkpoints`:

1. Look up wallet target (Section 6.1)
2. Build JSONB cursor from legacy fields (per P0-W3 Section 6)
3. Set `network` from Section 2.4
4. Set `source` from adapter type

---

## 7. Rollback Strategy

### 7.1 Phase 1 Rollback

- Remove dual-write logic (revert P1-W4)
- V2 tables can be dropped without V1 impact (no FKs from V1 to V2)
- V2 Rust types can be feature-gated or removed
- All V1 paths continue to function

### 7.2 Phase 2 Rollback

- Remove new API endpoints and CLI flags (additive, clean removal)
- Remove connector wrappers; restore direct `ChainIngestor` usage
- Disable dual-write; V1 tables still have all data
- Semantic corrections (EVM, Solana gRPC) evaluated individually

### 7.3 Point of No Return

Rollback becomes impractical once:
- `transactions` table stops receiving writes
- Read paths fully migrated to V2
- V1 tables dropped

This does not happen until Phase 4+ with explicit user approval.

---

## 8. Risk Register

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dual-write performance overhead | Medium | Medium | Benchmark; batch V2 writes; same DB transaction |
| V1/V2 data drift | Low | High | Reconciliation tests in P1-W5 and P2-W6 |
| EVM network reclassification | Medium | Medium | P1-W2 defines override mechanism |
| HyperCore timestamp precision loss | Low | Low | Dedup on `(network, tx_hash)` handles re-fetches |
| Legacy gRPC Solana checkpoint source | Low | Low | Default `source = "rpc"` safe for resume |

---

## 9. Decisions Locked By This Plan

| # | Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Additive migration strategy | New tables alongside old; no destructive changes | Wallet flows must keep working |
| 2 | Dual-write boundary is the repository layer | Not adapters or handlers | Single point of dual-write logic; adapters stay simple |
| 3 | V2 write failure does not block V1 write (early) | Best-effort V2 during early transition | De-risks Phase 1 rollout |
| 4 | Compatibility window closes no earlier than Phase 4 | Requires explicit user approval | Maximum safety for existing consumers |
| 5 | Wallet-to-target shim creates IndexTarget automatically | Transparent to V1 callers | Zero disruption for existing API/CLI users |
| 6 | Legacy checkpoints default to `source = "rpc"` | Per P0-W3 Section 6.2/6.5 | Safe for resume; gRPC gets fresh V2 checkpoints |
| 7 | Deprecation sequence matches P0-W1 Section 12 | Phase 1 soft, Phase 2 active, Phase 3+ removal | Gradual transition with clear milestones |
| 8 | Every Phase 1 and Phase 2 packet has explicit compat strategy | Section 4 of this document | No packet starts without a clear compatibility contract |

---

## 10. Cross-References

## 1. Compatibility Window

---

## 4. Per-Packet Compatibility Strategy

Every Phase 1 and Phase 2 work packet has an identified compatibility strategy.

### 4.1 Phase 1 Packets

#### P1-W1: Introduce V2 Core Types

**Strategy:** Additive types only. No existing types modified or removed. New
types (`ChainFamily`, `Network`, `IndexTarget`, `TargetKind`, `RawRecord`,
`Checkpoint`, `IngestionRun`, `Connector` trait) added alongside existing types.

**Unchanged:** `Chain`, `Transaction`, `IndexerCheckpoint`, `ChainIngestor`,
`LedgerEntry`, `EntryType`.

#### P1-W2: Add New Bronze And Control-Plane Tables

**Strategy:** Additive migrations only. New tables created alongside existing
tables. No existing table altered or dropped. New SQL enum types
(`chain_family_enum`, `target_kind_enum`, `target_mode_enum`) created as
separate types, not modifications to `chain_enum`.

**Unchanged:** All existing tables, columns, indexes, constraints, and enum types.

**Migration safety:** Must apply cleanly on empty DB and on top of current V1
schema. No `ALTER TABLE` on existing tables. No `DROP`.

#### P1-W3: Repository Support For Canonical Raw Data

**Strategy:** New repository methods added alongside existing ones. No existing
method signature changed.

**Unchanged:** All wallet-scoped read/write methods.

#### P1-W4: Dual-Write Compatibility Layer

**Strategy:** Repository layer modified so every V1 write also writes to V2
tables. The dual-write boundary is in the repository layer, not in adapters or
handlers.

**Dual-write flow (from P0-W1 Section 11.2):**
```
Ingestion request (wallet-shaped)
  |-- [compat shim] create IndexTarget(kind=wallet) if not exists
  |-- [compat shim] use old ChainIngestor::fetch_history
  |
  +-- write to `transactions` (V1)
  +-- write to `raw_transactions` (V2)
  +-- write to `target_matches` (V2)
  +-- write to `checkpoints` (V2)
  +-- write to `indexer_checkpoints` (V1)
```

**Unchanged:** All API handler signatures/responses. All CLI command
signatures/flags. All adapter `fetch_history` signatures. Read paths continue
to use V1 tables.

**Failure mode:** During early transition, V2 write failure does not block V1
write. Once V2 writes are proven stable, V1 write becomes best-effort.

#### P1-W5: Migration And Rollback Verification

**Strategy:** Verification-only packet. Validates fresh-DB and upgrade-DB
migration paths, cross-target linking, and rollback safety.

### 4.2 Phase 2 Packets

#### P2-W1: Connector Interface Redesign

**Strategy:** New `Connector` trait added alongside `ChainIngestor`. A
compatibility adapter wraps each `ChainIngestor` as a `Connector` that accepts
`IndexTarget(kind=wallet)` and delegates to `fetch_history`.

**Unchanged:** `ChainIngestor` trait and all implementations.

#### P2-W2: CLI And API Target Registration Flow

**Strategy:** New API endpoints and CLI flags added alongside existing ones.
Existing wallet-shaped requests accepted as before and internally create wallet
targets via compatibility shim.

**New endpoints (additive):** `POST /v1/targets`, `GET /v1/targets`,
`GET /v1/targets/:target_id`, `POST /v1/targets/:target_id/ingest`.

**New CLI flags (additive):** `--target-kind`, `--target-address`, `--network`.

**Unchanged:** `POST /v1/ingest`, `POST /v1/ingest/batch`, `--wallet` CLI flag.

#### P2-W3: Fix EVM Ingestion Semantics

**Strategy:** EVM adapter gains target-aware paths. Existing `fetch_history`
preserved as compatibility wrapper. Note: correcting EVM wallet semantics
changes data content (more correct results), not API surface.

**Unchanged:** `fetch_history` method signature.

#### P2-W4: Fix Solana gRPC Target Semantics

**Strategy:** Solana gRPC adapter gains target-aware subscription filters.
Existing `fetch_history` preserved as compatibility wrapper. Stops stamping
arbitrary wallet identity onto program-filtered results.

**Unchanged:** `fetch_history` method signature for backward compatibility.

#### P2-W5: Hyperliquid Target Model

**Strategy:** Hyperliquid adapters gain target-aware paths. Existing wallet/user
path preserved unchanged. Market targets and HyperEVM routing added as new
capabilities.

**Unchanged:** `fetch_history` for wallet/user targets.

#### P2-W6: End-To-End Ingestion Compatibility Suite

**Strategy:** Verification-only packet. Integration tests verify wallet targets
through V1 and V2 paths, new target types through V2 paths, dual-write
consistency, and checkpoint consistency.

## 6. Compatibility Shim Design

### 6.1 Wallet-to-Target Shim

When a V1 wallet-shaped request arrives:

1. Look up `index_targets` for `(kind=wallet, network=<derived>, address=<wallet>)`
2. If not found, create with `kind = wallet`, `network` from chain mapping
   (Section 2.4), `chain_family` derived from network, `address = <wallet>`,
   `mode = backfill`, `owner_id` from `user_id` if provided
3. Return target ID for V2 write paths

### 6.2 Transaction-to-RawRecord Shim

When adapter produces V1 `Transaction`:

1. Copy `id`, `timestamp`, `tx_hash`, `raw_metadata`
2. Map `chain` → `network` (Section 2.4)
3. Discard `user_id` and `wallet_address` (captured via `target_matches` and
   `index_targets.owner_id`)
4. Add `source` from adapter type

### 6.3 Checkpoint Shim

When repo writes V1 `indexer_checkpoints`:

1. Look up wallet target (Section 6.1)
2. Build JSONB cursor from legacy fields (per P0-W3 Section 6)
3. Set `network` from Section 2.4
4. Set `source` from adapter type

---

## 7. Rollback Strategy

### 7.1 Phase 1 Rollback

- Remove dual-write logic (revert P1-W4)
- V2 tables can be dropped without V1 impact (no FKs from V1 to V2)
- V2 Rust types can be feature-gated or removed
- All V1 paths continue to function

### 7.2 Phase 2 Rollback

- Remove new API endpoints and CLI flags (additive, clean removal)
- Remove connector wrappers; restore direct `ChainIngestor` usage
- Disable dual-write; V1 tables still have all data
- Semantic corrections (EVM, Solana gRPC) evaluated individually

### 7.3 Point of No Return

Rollback becomes impractical once:
- `transactions` table stops receiving writes
- Read paths fully migrated to V2
- V1 tables dropped

This does not happen until Phase 4+ with explicit user approval.

---

## 8. Risk Register

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dual-write performance overhead | Medium | Medium | Benchmark; batch V2 writes; same DB transaction |
| V1/V2 data drift | Low | High | Reconciliation tests in P1-W5 and P2-W6 |
| EVM network reclassification | Medium | Medium | P1-W2 defines override mechanism |
| HyperCore timestamp precision loss | Low | Low | Dedup on `(network, tx_hash)` handles re-fetches |
| Legacy gRPC Solana checkpoint source | Low | Low | Default `source = "rpc"` safe for resume |

---

## 9. Decisions Locked By This Plan

| # | Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Additive migration strategy | New tables alongside old; no destructive changes | Wallet flows must keep working |
| 2 | Dual-write boundary is the repository layer | Not adapters or handlers | Single point of dual-write logic; adapters stay simple |
| 3 | V2 write failure does not block V1 write (early) | Best-effort V2 during early transition | De-risks Phase 1 rollout |
| 4 | Compatibility window closes no earlier than Phase 4 | Requires explicit user approval | Maximum safety for existing consumers |
| 5 | Wallet-to-target shim creates IndexTarget automatically | Transparent to V1 callers | Zero disruption for existing API/CLI users |
| 6 | Legacy checkpoints default to `source = "rpc"` | Per P0-W3 Section 6.2/6.5 | Safe for resume; gRPC gets fresh V2 checkpoints |
| 7 | Deprecation sequence matches P0-W1 Section 12 | Phase 1 soft, Phase 2 active, Phase 3+ removal | Gradual transition with clear milestones |
| 8 | Every Phase 1 and Phase 2 packet has explicit compat strategy | Section 4 of this document | No packet starts without a clear compatibility contract |
